item.title: NEW: SonicWall Warns of Two Actively Exploited Zero-Days in SMA1000
item.description:
Headline: SonicWall Warns of Two Actively Exploited Zero-Days in SMA1000

Summary:
SonicWall has issued urgent patches for two zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549, affecting its SMA 1000 series appliances. The flaws, a critical server-side request forgery (SSRF) and a command injection, are being actively chained by threat actors to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. This marks the second time in seven weeks a similar SSRF-to-injection attack chain has targeted the product line, indicating a persistent architectural weakness. Organizations are urged to apply the patches immediately to prevent compromise.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Patch Management

Meta Description: SonicWall has patched two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities, including a critical SSRF (CVE-2026-83548), in its SMA 1000 series appliances.

Headline: Nutex Health Discloses Data Breach; 'The Gentlemen' Ransomware Claims Attack

Summary:
U.S. healthcare provider Nutex Health has disclosed a significant data breach in an SEC filing, stating that an unauthorized third party accessed and exfiltrated sensitive patient, employee, and business data. The notorious 'The Gentlemen' ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for the attack on its dark web leak site, threatening to publish the stolen information. The incident highlights the growing threat of Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operations targeting the healthcare sector with double-extortion tactics.

Headline: Google Patches Two Critical Use-After-Free Flaws in Chrome

Summary:
Google has released a security update for its Chrome browser, version 152.0.7977.75 for Windows/Mac and 152.0.7977.76 for Linux, addressing 26 vulnerabilities. The patch includes fixes for two critical use-after-free flaws, CVE-2026-84353 in Shared Tab Groups and CVE-2026-84352 in WebGL. These vulnerabilities could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on a victim's device by luring them to a malicious website. Google reports no evidence of active exploitation.

Headline: FBI Warns of Sophisticated OAuth Consent Phishing Campaign

Summary:
The FBI has issued a public service announcement about an ongoing and sophisticated phishing campaign active since late 2025. Attackers are using a technique called 'OAuth consent phishing' to gain persistent, password-independent access to the cloud accounts of prominent individuals, their families, and associates. The campaign involves impersonating officials or journalists to trick targets into granting malicious applications access to their Microsoft or Google accounts.

item.title: NEW: EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-Hour Breach Reporting Deadline Looms
item.description:
Headline: EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-Hour Breach Reporting Deadline Looms

Summary:
A key compliance milestone for the EU's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is approaching on September 11, 2026. From that date, manufacturers of products with digital elements sold in the EU market must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents to authorities within 24 hours of becoming aware of them. This stringent deadline marks a significant shift towards mandatory, rapid disclosure and requires organizations to have mature incident response processes in place.

Severity: Informational

Categories: Policy and Compliance, Regulatory

item.description:
Headline: Critical JFrog Artifactory Auth Bypass Flaw Actively Exploited

Summary:
A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-82329, in JFrog Artifactory is being actively exploited in the wild, just days after a patch was released. The flaw, which has a CVSS score of 9.8, allows an unauthenticated attacker to abuse a default configuration weakness to forge administrator-level tokens. This provides full control over the artifact repository, posing a severe software supply chain security risk as attackers could poison binaries and compromise downstream users.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Supply Chain Attack, Cyberattack

item.title: NEW: Education Sector Faces Highest Cyberattack Intensity: SonicWall Report
item.description:
Headline: Education Sector Faces Highest Cyberattack Intensity: SonicWall Report

Summary:
A new report from SonicWall reveals the education sector suffered the highest per-device attack intensity of any industry in the first half of 2026. A single VoIP exploitation signature accounted for over half of all intrusion events. The sector's uniquely open networks, combined with a prevalence of unpatched systems running vulnerable software like Log4j and old Hikvision IP camera firmware, make it a prime target for a wide range of cyberattacks, including ransomware from groups like Ryuk.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Intelligence, Cyberattack, Ransomware

Meta Description: A new SonicWall report finds the education sector suffered the highest intensity of cyberattacks in H1 2026, driven by VoIP exploits and unpatched vulnerabilities.

item.title: NEW: Unit 42 Details First Ransomware Attack Using Autonomous AI Agents
item.description:
Headline: Unit 42 Details First Ransomware Attack Using Autonomous AI Agents

Summary:
Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has published a detailed investigation into a ransomware attack where the threat actor leveraged frontier AI models and autonomous agentic frameworks. This pioneering attack methodology allowed the adversary to compress weeks of complex intrusion activities into less than ten hours. After gaining initial access, the AI agents autonomously mapped the victim's internal network, exfiltrated source code from repositories, seized root credentials, and compromised the cloud AI infrastructure by triggering unauthorized CI/CD builds. The report highlights a significant evolution in cyber threats, where AI-driven operational efficiency, rather than novel zero-day exploits, enables rapid and scalable attacks.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Ransomware, Cyberattack

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 4 minutes

Meta Description: Unit 42 investigates a pioneering cyber attack where an attacker deployed autonomous AI agents for a ransomware operation, breaching a network in under 10 hours.

item.title: UPDATE: Attackers Hijack AI API Keys to Fuel Gray Market "Transfer Stations"
item.description:
Headline: Attackers Hijack AI API Keys to Fuel Gray Market "Transfer Stations"

Summary:
A new threat dubbed "token jacking" has emerged where attackers steal AI API keys from developers to power illicit "transfer stations." These gray market services resell access to premium AI models at a fraction of the cost, often fueled by stolen credentials. Attackers are using methods like information stealers, phishing, and malicious npm packages to harvest API tokens. The financial impact can be severe, as attackers can consume vast amounts of AI computing resources before the theft is detected, leading to massive bills for the victim organizations. This highlights the urgent need for robust security around AI development environments.

Severity: High

Categories: Cloud Security, Threat Intelligence, Supply Chain Attack

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 8 minutes

Meta Description: Cybercriminals are stealing AI API keys in a new attack trend called 'token jacking' to power illicit services, resulting in significant financial losses. Learn how they do it and how to protect your AI resources.

item.title: UPDATE: Threat Actors Use AI Scripts to Target Siemens PLCs in Critical Infrastructure
item.description:
Headline: Threat Actors Use AI Scripts to Target Siemens PLCs in Critical Infrastructure

Summary:
A joint advisory from U.S. agencies like the NSA and CISA warns of an ongoing campaign where threat actors are using AI-generated scripts to target Siemens S7 Series Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) in U.S. critical infrastructure. The attackers are using scanning tools to find exposed PLCs and then deploying malicious scripts, created with the help of AI and open-source libraries, to conduct reconnaissance. This activity suggests a pre-positioning for future disruptive attacks. The campaign affects a wide range of Siemens PLCs across sectors like energy, water, and manufacturing. Agencies urge asset owners to isolate these devices from the internet and apply patches.

Severity: High

Categories: Industrial Control Systems, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 5 minutes

item.description:
Headline: McKesson Discloses Breach After ShinyHunters Claims Patient Data Theft

Summary:
U.S. healthcare giant McKesson has confirmed a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized network access and data exfiltration. The ShinyHunters extortion group has claimed responsibility, alleging the theft of approximately one terabyte of data, including 284 million patient-related records, from a Snowflake environment. The breach was discovered on August 25, 2026, with the data exfiltration reportedly occurring over the preceding four days. McKesson has acknowledged the incident in an SEC filing but has not yet determined its full material impact. The investigation is ongoing, and the company has warned customers of potential service degradation.
